target: lien.finance (BondMaker + GeneralizedDotc OTC pools, Ethereum mainnet)
methodology: forensics of real exploit (tx 0xb96d572b..., block 25599302, ~542K USDC) -> source pull (LienFinance/bondmaker) -> on-chain group/bond enumeration -> replay of the full 5-tx attacker sequence on anvil fork at block 25599301 with debug_traceTransaction (callTracer) -> drain confirmed -> writeup

0x843225CF6e663e4454732D6B551A737Ac7b47d.note: deployed version differs from repo main: issueNewBonds(uint256,uint256) selector 125d8583 NOT in bytecode

root_cause: Duplicate bond IDs in registered bond groups pass _assertBondGroup value checks and are minted multiple times by exchangeEquivalentBonds, creating uncollateralized bonds

_checkExceptionBonds is an aggregate occurrence-count check (count == exceptionBonds.length), not a multiset/coverage check — exceptions that do not cover the input group still pass, skipping required burns
_calcRateBondToErc20 prices strike-0 IMT/LBT bonds at full collateral value; GeneralizedDotc pools pay USDC from LP standing allowance
final_verdict: VULNERABLE (reproduced) — the deployed BondMaker/GeneralizedDotc code is exploitable exactly as the 2026-07-24 attacker did; full drain (542,144.63 USDC) reproduced on a forked chain at the pre-exploit block. Protocols remain live/unpatched on mainnet (no pause circuitry).
method_note: Selector-grep heuristics flagged only generic mint/transfer surfaces; the real vulnerability (logic/accounting bypass) required replaying the actual exploit with a state-machine orchestration on an archive fork. This is a strong validation target for the defihunter toolkit's replay capability.
